reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care for the Israelites through multiple manifestations: (1) God hears their cries and groaning under Egyptian slavery (וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָם); (2) God remembers His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ בְּרִיתוֹ); (3) God sees the Israelites and acknowledges their situation (וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֵּדַע); (4) God promises comprehensive liberation: 'I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians... and I will redeem you' (וְהוֹצֵאתִי...וְהִצַּלְתִּי...וְגָאַלְתִּי); (5) God declares 'I will take you as my people and I will be your God' (וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים); and (6) God promises to bring them to the land sworn to their ancestors. These actions collectively constitute explicit expressions of divine care, responsiveness to suffering, and commitment to the welfare of His people.
